purpose.description: Define target functions used to evaluate interface sufficiency in the canonical linear system.
purpose.role: Specify what information must be preserved by an observation interface.
purpose.principle: Identifiability is target-relative; an interface may be sufficient for one target and insufficient for another.

targets.name: Future first-coordinate prediction
targets.semantic_description: Predict the first state coordinate after five transitions.

dependency.reason: Both coordinates enter the scalar target through the linear functional e_1^T A^5.

targets.note: A one-dimensional target-aligned projection is sufficient for this scalar target.

targets.name: Current first-coordinate observation
targets.semantic_description: Read the current first state coordinate.

targets.name: Future second-coordinate prediction
targets.semantic_description: Predict the hidden second state coordinate after evolution.

target_equivalence_relation.definition: Two states are equivalent for target L when they produce identical target values.
target_equivalence_relation.importance: Observation equivalence must refine target equivalence.

decision.meaning: Targets define the observable quantities against which candidate interfaces are evaluated.

notes: The benchmark intentionally separates system complexity from target complexity.
A richer target requires a richer interface.
Interface sufficiency is never absolute; it is always relative to a specified target.
